messages.subject: More factor questions; also, strange error message.
messages.subject_clean: More factor questions; also, strange error message.
messages.body_plain:
Dear Gabor--

The code below is intended to test whether, when sqldf/SQLite reads a long vector from a file connection – longer than the chunks SQLite uses when reading from that connection – into a database, , it succeeds in picking up the late-occurring factor levels of vectors that are factors – levels that occur only after it has read the initial chunk.

This is part of a project to read a large(20 gig) csv file into a data base. I will be doing a great deal of work with this file over a period of years, and I want to get formats and such right in the database so I do not have to worry about type conversions and perform them over and over each time I grab a variable. Thus if at all possible I want the factors to be correctly described in the database, and returned from the database by sqldf with the correct type, without further post-processing or modification.

 I want the database file to be permanent, not transient, so for my test I fairly slavishly followed this example: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2010-October/257270.html, which you refer to in example number 6 on your google code page.

 The only difference between this example and my code, copied below, that I can see is in the variable names and the size and shape of the data frame, and that I have added method="name__class" at the end of the CREATE TABLE command. However, your code runs and mine does not. This is true even if I run one right after the other, regardless of order. I saw your warning about keyword conflicts in FAQ 2 and tried changing the names of all my variables, twice, to no avail. Similarly with taking out the method parameter. Every effort to get data out of the data base ends in this error message:
“Error in sqliteExecStatement(con, statement, bind.data) :
  RS-DBI driver: (error in statement: no such table: xtest01)”

Can you tell me where my code is going wrong?

# sqldf & late-occuring factor levels

# Make a toy example of a csv file containing numeric and character data (to be represented as a factors) containing a late-occuring level.

# Based on this example by Gabor Grothendieck:    https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2010-October/257270.html

 require(sqldf)
require(tcltk)

rowN__integer <- 1:50001
aaLevels__factor <- as.character(c(rep(c(6:10), times=10000), 99))
bb__integer <- c(rep(c(1:5), times=10000), 6)
testIt <- data.frame(rowN__integer, aaLevels__factor, bb__integer)
write.table(testIt, file="testIt.csv", quote=FALSE, sep=",", row.names=FALSE)

# read the file into an SQLite database. Read each variable back into R and
# test whether level="99" is in the output.

# The next 3 commands persuade sqldf that it hasn't created the file. <How?>
testCon <- file("testIt.csv")
attr(testCon, "file.format")  <- list(header=TRUE, sep=",", eol="\r\n") # eol=0D0A (\r\n)
sqldf("attach 'xtestDB' as new")

## read testCon into xtest01 table of xtestDB database
sqldf("create table xtest01 as select * from testCon", dbname = "xtestDB"), method="name__class")

## check that its there
sqldf("select * from sqlite_master", dbname = "xtestDB")
sqldf("select count(*) from xtest01", dbname = "mydb")
sqldf(".table")

# Return aaLevels & bb, check class, length, head, tail, levels(aaLevels) for errors.
# Relace levels with labels, and assign corrected factor back to aaLevels. Repeat tests.

aaLabels <-c("eeny", "meeny", "larry", "curly", "miney", "mo")
out.DF <- sqldf("SELECT aaLevels, bb, rowN FROM xtable01  ORDER BY rowN", dbname="testDB")
tail(out.DF, 5)

I am running this code under MS-Windows XP with SP3, on RStudio, using R 3.0.1.
capabilities()[["tcltk"]] evaluates as true.

Any help you could offer would be greatly appreciated.

Sincerely,   andrewH

P.S. My data set has numeric codes, analogous to R’s internal representation of factors, for factor-like variables. It also has short descriptions, often numeric ranges, that correspond to R’s factor labels. If the data file was small enough to read into memory, I would define the numeric codes as factor levels, and use the factor “labels” parameter to recode them to the correct levels provided. That way I would only have to do it once, instead of every time I needed to read the variable.

 I gather that SQLite makes it difficult to extract a column, process it, and replace it, so I would need to replace levels with labels for each of the 200-odd factor variables when reading those variables into the database.  In other words, I understand that I can not read the variables in from a file and replace the levels _in the database_ with the labels so as to get the corrected values of the levels (i.e. the labels) in a subsequent step. Is that correct, or am I misinformed? If I tell sqldf that selected variables are factors using the sqldf method parameter, does it then expect to receive a character vector with the values equal to the corresponding label, like labels(X)[X] for X a factor? Or does it expect consecutive integers like R’s internal representation of factors? If the latter, and data is coming from a file connection rather than a data frame, how do you get the levels into the database?

If you intend to keep the data in the database then sqldf may not be the best fit.  Its more for using SQL with R data.frames.  You would be better off using RSQLite directly (or the corresponding interface to whatevr database you decide upon.

There were a few errors in the code including getting the database or table name wrong. ".table" is not an SQL statement (".tables" is an sqlite3 console directive which is not itself SQL). You don't need require(tcltk).  There were some missing __integer, etc.  The code below gives me no errors when run.

The statement 'aaLabels <-c("eeny", "meeny", "larry", "curly", "miney", "mo")' has no effect in this code.

SQLite does not support factor/enum types at all and the only reason we get a factor in this example is that sqldf will do some post processing on the output depending on the method= used.

One can use the update SQL statement to modify columns in place as shown below.

library(sqldf)

rowN__integer <- 1:50001
aaLevels__factor <- as.character(c(rep(c(6:10), times=10000), 99))
bb__integer <- c(rep(c(1:5), times=10000), 6)
testIt <- data.frame(rowN__integer, aaLevels__factor, bb__integer)
write.table(testIt, file="testIt.csv", quote=FALSE, sep=",", row.names=FALSE)

# read the file into an SQLite database. Read each variable back into R and
# test whether level="99" is in the output.

# The next 3 commands persuade sqldf that it hasn't created the file. <How?>
testCon <- file("testIt.csv")
attr(testCon, "file.format")  <- list(header=TRUE, sep=",", eol="\r\n") # eol=0D0A (\r\n)
sqldf("attach 'xtestDB' as new")

## read testCon into xtest01 table of xtestDB database

sqldf("create table xtest01 as select * from testCon", dbname = "xtestDB", method="name__class")

## check that its there
sqldf("select * from sqlite_master", dbname = "xtestDB")

sqldf("select count(*) from xtest01", dbname = "xtestDB")
sqldf("pragma table_info(xtest01)", dbname = "xtestDB")

out.DF <- sqldf("
  SELECT aaLevels__factor, bb__integer, rowN__integer
  FROM xtest01
  ORDER BY rowN__integer",
  dbname="xtestDB", method = "name__class")

tail(out.DF, 5)

sqldf("update xtest01 set aaLevels__factor = case
   when aaLevels__factor = 6 then 'level6'
   when aaLevels__factor = 7 then 'level7'
   when aaLevels__factor = 8 then 'level8'
   when aaLevels__factor = 9 then 'level9'
   when aaLevels__factor = 10 then 'level10'
   else '99'
end", dbname = "xtestDB")
